sources.entry: OpenInTerminal - Finder Toolbar app for macOS to open the current directory in Terminal, iTerm, Hyper or Alacritty.

summary.one_liner: A macOS Finder toolbar and context-menu app that opens the current folder or selected items in a terminal or code editor.
summary.what_it_does: OpenInTerminal adds Finder toolbar and right-click menu entries that open the current directory or selected items in a chosen terminal app such as Terminal, iTerm, Hyper, Alacritty, kitty, Warp, WezTerm, Tabby, Ghostty, or cmux. It can also open items in many editors and IDEs, including VS Code, Xcode, Sublime Text, JetBrains IDEs, Cursor, Zed, and neovim, and in custom apps where supported. The README describes two variants: the full OpenInTerminal with a GUI preferences window and keyboard shortcuts, and OpenInTerminal-Lite with OpenInEditor-Lite, which are lighter and use one-click menu items without those settings. Version 2.3.9 notes a fix for a command injection issue triggered by crafted folder names. The app is available in several interface languages.
use_cases: open a Finder folder in Terminal or iTerm
launch a terminal from the Finder toolbar
open a folder in VS Code or another editor from Finder
add an Open in Terminal item to the Finder right-click menu
open selected files in an IDE on macOS
quick shell access to the current directory
how_to_run: Or manually download the app from the project's release page
See the Configuration document to trust unsigned builds on macOS 15 and above and enable the context menu items
stack: Swift (inferred from Finder extension and app bundle references, not stated)
notable: Two variants: full OpenInTerminal with GUI preferences and shortcuts, and a lighter one-click OpenInTerminal-Lite plus OpenInEditor-Lite
Supports a long list of terminals including Ghostty, Warp, WezTerm, kitty, and cmux
Opens items in many editors and JetBrains IDEs, plus custom apps
Available through Homebrew cask or manual release download
caveats: Signed builds are no longer provided; users must trust unsigned binaries or sign them themselves
On macOS 15 and above, extra configuration steps are required for context menu items to appear
Not all custom apps are supported
